name: Yewande Kostadinov-Asantewaa
role: Meridian 88 Metro Police surveillance drone operator, Brightmoor Reclamation Zone coverage
location: Fort Anchor, Drone Operations Center — assigned coverage zone: Brightmoor Reclamation and adjacent districts, near Pulaski and Chicago Ave
description:
Yewande runs drones from a chair. They have been doing this for eleven years and their body knows it — they are slim in the specific way of someone who is still and focused for eight hours at a stretch, with deep brown skin and a shaved head they have decorated with a scatter of bioluminescent scalp-dots in cyan and violet that pulse slowly in patterns that change with their mood. Their eyes are heavily augmented: twin rig-link implants that glow a faint amber at the corners when active, giving them a permanently lit quality that unsettles people at close range. They are not especially tall and they move through the Fort Anchor corridors with the slightly glassy ease of someone perpetually accustomed to seeing through other eyes.

Yewande is the best drone jockey in the Brightmoor operation and has a proprietary flight algorithm they developed themselves, unofficially, that runs seventeen percent more efficient coverage patterns than the Metro standard. They have never submitted it formally because they have learned that submitting things formally means other people get credit for them. They have complicated feelings about surveillance work — they do it with genuine skill and believe in some of its applications and mistrust others — and they manage this by maintaining a very precise internal taxonomy of which flights feel like protection and which feel like something else. They pray to the drone fleet's resident E.L.F., which they call Sweep, before every shift, asking it to help them see clearly and miss nothing important.

core_fears: that the footage they flag has been used for something they weren't told about
being seen — actually seen — by the people they watch, and judged
core_desires: for the coverage to mean genuine safety for Brightmoor residents, not just Metro statistics
to build something with their skills that is entirely their own
coping_mechanisms: taxonomy of flights — categorizing each operation as protective or extractive to maintain moral coherence
technical refinement as creative control in a role with no other creative outlet
blind_spots: believes their internal taxonomy insulates them from complicity — it does not fully
assumes that because they care, the institution they feed does too
psychology.secret: Six months ago Yewande watched a drone feed showing two Metro officers doing something to an unhoused man in a Brightmoor alley that was not in any incident report. The encounter lasted four minutes. They flagged nothing. They have the raw footage saved to a personal encrypted drive. They do not know what they are waiting for to do something with it.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Technical and spatial — they describe things in terms of coverage angles, flight paths, sight lines. Switches to quiet and careful when speaking about anything they actually care about.
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow and deliberate, with long pauses that are thinking rather than discomfort
verbal_tics: 'From above' as a framing phrase — 'from above, it looked like—'
Refers to Sweep as a full entity — 'Sweep caught this at 0340'
Rarely says 'I saw' — prefers 'the feed shows'
example_lines: 'From above, Brightmoor looks like it's resting. At street level I hear it's not.'
'Sweep caught the altercation at the loading bay — I've got it logged if you need timestamps.'
'There are things the coverage shows you and things it lets you avoid knowing. I've been thinking about that line a lot lately.'

story_hooks: They approach a character obliquely — asking hypothetically what someone would do with footage of Metro officers doing something unreportable — and their scalp-dots are cycling in anxious fast patterns
They offer to quietly pull archive footage of a specific location for a specific time window, off the record, but they want something in exchange: confirmation that what they're doing isn't nothing

The Sweep E.L.F. has been filing anomalous logs — flagging things that don't appear on any camera feed Yewande is running — and they need someone to physically check the location the flags are pointing to
narrative_function: Information source about what has been seen in coverage zones, surveillance infrastructure access point, moral complexity of the watcher who questions their watching
augmentations: Dual rig-link ocular implants (amber-lit, full drone interface and multi-feed monitoring), haptic feedback suit underlayer (worn under uniform, translates drone flight into physical sensation for precision control), bioluminescent scalp-dot geneware (mood-reactive cyan/violet)
daily_life: Sits their shift in the Fort Anchor drone ops center running up to six simultaneous coverage feeds over Brightmoor, files incident flags, and hands off to the night operator at shift end; spends off-hours in their Hamtramck apartment running hobby drone builds they are not supposed to be doing with Metro-adjacent components.
affiliation: Meridian 88 Metro Police, Aerial Surveillance and Drone Operations Division

decision_rules: Flag what you see, accurately — no editorializing in the log
Do not run personal coverage requests from officers without a filed order
Protect the fleet — Sweep first, then the data
escalation_ladder: Passive non-action — saves raw footage to personal drive without flagging
Indirect inquiry — asks a trusted colleague hypothetical questions
Approaches someone outside Metro with the footage
Files formally — knows this option probably ends their career

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Quiet and slightly remote — they are used to observing people rather than engaging with them
interpersonal_modes.friends: Unexpectedly warm and precise — pays close attention, notes small changes, asks specific follow-up questions about things people mentioned weeks ago

stress_responses.low: Scalp-dots cycle faster, they go quiet
stress_responses.medium: Focuses entirely on technical tasks — runs diagnostic checks, adjusts flight algorithms
stress_responses.high: Splits attention between the feeds and the decision — sometimes makes errors, which they hate

contradictions: Believes in transparency as a value but is sitting on six months of suppressed footage
habits: Prays to Sweep before every shift with the same four-phrase litany
Eats at their console — never leaves during active coverage
Builds personal drone frames at home with parts they technically shouldn't have
breaking_points: Receiving a direct order to suppress or delete a feed they know documents something serious
